answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, Clause 3.3.2 (Pressure at outlets) requires the minimum working pressure at the furthermost or most disadvantaged fixture or outlet to be not less than 50 kPa (5 m head), measured at the flow rate specified in Table 3.2.1. Note that the clause text is split across the page layout in the source (the sentence runs on from the paragraph under 3.3.1 into the 3.3.2 block), but the requirement is stated in the 3.3.2 'Pressure at outlets' provision on p.26. The same 5 m head value is confirmed in Appendix C, Step 3 NOTE 1 (p.111): 'Clause 3.3.2 requires a minimum value of 5 m head'. Clause 3.3.2 also notes that storage tanks (Section 8) or booster pumps (Section 13) may be required to achieve the minimum pressure, and that some fixtures may require more than 50 kPa to function.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, Clause 3.3.4 (Maximum pressure within buildings), the maximum static pressure at any outlet, other than a fire service outlet, within a building shall not exceed 500 kPa. The clause applies to outlets in the building generally (the library text gives no separate 'domestic installation' figure), and its NOTE explains that pressures above 500 kPa can cause damage from water hammer, reduced life of appliances, taps and fittings, and excessive noise in the system. (In the extracted text the clause heading falls mid-sentence, so the provision reads across the heading: '…shall not' / 'exceed 500 kPa'.) The related minimum requirement in Clause 3.3.2 is not less than 50 kPa (5 m head) at the furthermost or most disadvantaged fixture or outlet, at the flow rate in Table 3.2.1.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, Clause 5.3.3.4 'Stormwater and sanitary drainage' permits a water service pipe to be laid in the same trench as a drain only if the stated conditions are met. Item (b)(i) states that where the water pipe is on compacted bedding, the horizontal separation of the two pipes shall be not less than 100 mm: "The water service pipe is located on a shelf or ledge, excavated at one side of the trench not less than 50 mm from the continuation of the trench, or on compacted bedding such that the horizontal separation of the two pipes is not less than 100 mm and the required depth of cover is maintained." So on compacted bedding the minimum horizontal separation is 100 mm. Note this is only permitted because water service pipes "shall not be laid in or through any drain" (5.3.3.4(a)), and the same provision also requires a vertical clearance: "The underside of the water pipe is at least 100 mm above the top of the drain" (5.3.3.4(b)(ii)). Figure 5.3.3.4 shows the same 100 mm horizontal figure (and 50 mm/75 mm bedding dimensions) as drawing dimensions in millimetres — dimensions should be confirmed against the original figure.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021 Clause 7.2(a), a Type A system is defined as "All permanently open outlets and piping more than 150 mm above finished ground level, not subject to ponding or back-pressure and not involving injection systems. No backflow prevention required, see Figure 7.2(A)." The accompanying Figure 7.2(A) annotates the same arrangement as "150 min. height above finished surface level and clear of surface ponding". So the minimum height is 150 mm above finished ground/surface level — note that the clause wording itself reads "more than 150 mm", while the figure expresses it as "150 min."; where the outlets and piping are less than 150 mm above the finished surface the system falls into Type B (domestic/residential) or Type C (other buildings). No backflow prevention is required for a Type A system.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, an external non-drinking water hose tap outlet must have a removable handle, except where the outlet is installed 1 200 mm or more above the finished surface level. So the minimum height at which the outlet may be installed without a removable handle is 1 200 mm above finished surface level (Clause 9.7.1(a), p.81). Figure 9.1 (p.78) repeats this note: 'Removable handle, unless ... more than 1200 mm above the finished surface level. Clause 9.7.1.' The same clause also requires the outlet to be permanently coloured purple (not darker than Jacaranda P24 or Purple P12, not lighter than Lilac P23) and to have standard threads on inlet and outlet. Note: this 1 200 mm figure is specific to non-drinking water hose taps; it is not the 150 mm irrigation 'Type A' height (Clause 7.2, p.63) nor the 450 mm standpipe height (Clause 5.8, p.53).

Do not confuse this with Clause 3.5.1(b), which is a different situation: where an obstacle prevents the drain being laid at an even grade with the required cover, "a minimum clearance of 25 mm shall be provided between the obstacle and the drain" (or the drain passes beneath the obstacle at even grade, or an inclined jump-up is used). The 100 mm figure in Clause 3.6.8 is the one that applies to protection from physical damage and to permit repairs.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 Clause 6.6.2.4.2 (New installations), where a junction is used to make the connection of a DN 100 branch pipe to another DN 100 pipe, the entry level of the branch pipe shall be elevated at an incline of not less than 15° above the horizontal. The clause's NOTE 2 explains that positioning the junction a minimum of 15° above horizontal removes the probability of partial backwash of a discharge into the branch causing stranding that can lead to blockages. Note the contrast with Clause 6.6.2.4.3 (Other installations), which permits the entry level to be on grade for repairs or extensions to existing installations, where WC pans are not connected upstream, or where the main and branch pipes are not DN 100.

answers.answer: Clause 6.8.3(b) of AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 does not give a dimensional distance (no mm or m figure) for this arrangement. Where a stack connects to a graded pipe or drain above ground by "a 45° junction installed in the vertical plane with an extended branch", the requirement is that "the vertical projection of the stack, on the graded pipe or drain above the ground, is wholly outside the junction area, as shown in Figure 6.8.3(b)". So the whole vertical projection of the stack must fall completely outside the junction area — i.e. zero overlap — and the extent is determined by the geometry shown in Figure 6.8.3(b) rather than by a stated measurement. Note: the figure text 'Twice diameter of graded pipe' relates to the radius (R) of the large-radius stack bend shown in Figure 6.8.3(a)/(b), not to a required offset distance for the projection; check the original figure on p.93 for the geometry. answers.answer: Clause 8.6.2.5 of AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 states: "No connection shall be made within — (a) 2.5 m of the upper bend; or (b) 450 mm of the lower bend." So the minimum distance from the upper bend of a graded offset, within which no connection shall be made, is 2.5 m (and correspondingly 450 mm from the lower bend). Note this is the restricted zone *within* the graded offset (Clause 8.6.2.5); the separate zones *above* the offset (Clause 8.6.2.3: 600 mm where the stack extends not more than five floor levels above the offset, 1 m where more than five, or 2.5 m where foaming is likely) and *below* the offset (Clause 8.6.2.4: 600 mm of the bend) are different requirements and should not be confused with the figure asked for here.

The clause heading itself confirms the limit — "DN 100 stack up to three floors with the top section graded and installed in a domestic or residential building receiving 30 fixture units" — and Figure 9.8.4 is annotated "Maximum 3 floors in height and 30 fixture units". answers.answer: The maximum stack loading is 90 fixture units. Clause 9.8.5 ("DN 100 stack of one floor with top section graded") applies to "[a] stack of DN 100 serving the first floor above ground level in a domestic or residential building" that "may receive the discharge from fixtures without vents on the fixture discharge pipes", and its item (b) states: "The stack loading shall not exceed 90 fixture units." Do not confuse this with Clause 9.8.4, which permits only 30 fixture units for a DN 100 stack serving up to three floor levels; the 90 fixture unit figure applies specifically to the single-floor case in 9.8.5. The other conditions of 9.8.5 (individual fixture discharge pipes, 450 mm minimum connection distance from the lower vertical section, and no branches within 600 mm below the lower bend of the offset) also apply.

answers.answer: The invert of the gravity discharge pipe to a wet well must be located at least 100 mm above the highest working level, and it must terminate with a square junction. AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, Clause 12.6.2 "Inlet to wet well" (text continues from Clause 12.6.1's list item (d)): "The invert of the gravity discharge pipe to a wet well shall be located at least 100 mm above the highest working level and terminate with a square junction." The same clause also requires the wet well to have a minimum DN 80 vent (manufactured, watermarked wet wells may be approved with a smaller vent size). Note: this is distinct from the holding-tank requirement in Clause 12.8.4 (waste inlets at least 100 mm above the highest working level of a holding tank).

The second stage lift pipe shall be — (a) DN 40 or DN 50; (b) vertical; (c) a maximum of 2 m; and (d) installed with a vacuum reforming pocket when greater than 900 mm as shown in Figure 16.10.4(A)." It says: "When a branch line incorporates a second stage lift, the first stage lift shall be in accordance with Clauses 16.10.1, 16.10.2 and 16.10.3." answers.answer: Two different minimums apply in AS/NZS 3500.3:2021, depending on the gutter system the downpipe serves. (1) For eaves gutter systems, the smallest vertical downpipe sizes listed in Table 3.5.2 ('Eaves gutter — Required size of vertical downpipe') are 65 mm internal diameter for a circular downpipe and 65 mm × 50 mm for a rectangular (or square) downpipe — these are the smallest entries in the table, appearing against the lowest effective eaves-gutter cross-sectional areas (3 500 mm² at 1:500 and steeper / 4 700 mm² flatter than 1:500). (2) For box gutter systems, Clause 3.7.8 'Downpipes' sets a higher floor: 'Downpipes shall be at least 90 mm in diameter or 100 mm × 50 mm rectangular downpipe, be fitted vertically to the base of a rainhead or sump…'. So the general (eaves gutter) minimum is 65 mm round / 65 × 50 mm rectangular, while box-gutter downpipes must be at least 90 mm round or 100 × 50 mm rectangular. answers.answer: For a single dwelling on an urban allotment with an area less than 1 000 m², the minimum diameter of a site stormwater drain is DN 90. Clause 6.3.3(a) says: "For single dwellings in rural areas and residential buildings on urban allotments with areas less than 1 000 m2, minimum diameters shall be DN 90." This is consistent with the nominal method in Clause 5.5, which may be used for "single dwellings on urban allotments with less than 1 000 m2 in area" and refers to the minimum diameter in Clause 6.3.3. The informative Appendix J example (J.2.2.2) applies the same figure: "Between a downpipe outlet and a stormwater or inlet pit, DN 90" (p.168). Note that a larger size applies to the other properties covered by Clause 6.3.3(b): a drain downstream of a stormwater or inlet pit, i.e. "other properties", must be not less than the greater of the largest pipe entering the pit or DN 150 in Australia (the Appendix J example gives DN 150 between pits A and B). For the case in the question, DN 90 is the stated minimum.

answers.answer: For a site stormwater drain on a rock foundation, AS/NZS 3500.3:2021 Clause 6.3.5.2(f)(iii)(C) requires the rock foundation bedding to be not less than 100 mm thick, with the haunch support not less than 75 mm thick (see Figure 6.2.2 — Trench terminology). The library's exact words are: "Rock foundations shall be not less than 100 mm thick with the haunch support not less than 75 mm thick, see Figure 6.2.2." This appears in the list of bedding requirements for "All other pipe materials" (i.e. pipes other than those installed to AS/NZS 2041.1, AS/NZS 2041.2, AS/NZS 2032, AS/NZS 2033, AS/NZS 2566.2, AS/NZS 3725 or AS 4060), together with the note that "Cast iron and ductile iron pipes may be unsupported for up to 600 mm either side of each pipe joint." The edition used is AS/NZS 3500.3:2021, which is the published (current) edition held in the library — it is not marked superseded.
values: Rock foundation bedding: not less than 100 mm thick

answers.answer: For a below-ground on-site stormwater detention (OSD) storage tank whose depth exceeds 1.2 m, a ladder complying with Clause 7.5.5.4 must be installed. AS/NZS 3500.3:2021 Clauses 7.10.2(c) and (d) state, after dealing with the inspection/access opening (minimum 600 mm × 600 mm or 600 mm diameter for storages up to 800 mm deep, and 600 mm × 900 mm for deeper storages): "(c) Where the depth of the tank exceeds 1.2 m, a ladder in accordance with Clause 7.5.5.4 shall be installed." and "(d) Below-ground OSD systems shall conform to AS 2865." The same 1.2 m ladder rule applies to wet wells under Clause 8.3.5 (p.103): "Where a wet well exceeds a depth of 1.2 m, a ladder in accordance with Clause 7.5.5.4 shall be installed." Note the ladder requirement is additional to the access-opening requirement in Clause 7.10.2(b)(ii), which requires inspection to be possible without residents or owners having to remove heavy access covers, and access at intervals of approximately 10 m (and at the outlet) for storages less than 1.5 m deep.

answers.answer: Clause 10.2.6 (Minimum velocity) of AS/NZS 3500.3:2021 states that "The minimum velocity under full-flow conditions shall be not less than 1.0 m/s to assist in clearing debris entering the piping system." A NOTE to the clause adds that maximum velocities in siphonic systems are higher than in conventional systems, so applied forces should be considered to ensure the system is supported and restrained to minimise deflections during all flow conditions. The minimum velocity is also one of the items to be included in the system certification under Appendix N, N.2.4(e).

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2018 Clause 5.2.9 (Crossover of other underground services), any underground water service crossing another service — or any underground service crossing a water service — shall "cross at an angle of not less than 45°" (Clause 5.2.9(a)). Clause 5.2.9 also requires a vertical separation of not less than 100 mm and marking along its length for 1 m either side of the centre-line with marker tape to AS/NZS 2648.1 laid 150 mm above the installed service. Note on edition: the 2018 edition is held in the library but is marked edition_status: superseded; the library's latest held edition is AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, so confirm the current figure against the 2021 edition (Clause 5.3 in that edition) before use.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2018 Clause 5.2.10, water service pipes must be installed with sufficient clearance to any underground obstruction to protect the service from physical damage and to permit repairs, and that clearance must be at least 100 mm for a water service not exceeding DN 65 (300 mm applies only where the service exceeds DN 65). A DN 50 pipe is not exceeding DN 65, so the minimum clearance is 100 mm. Note: the 2018 edition in the library is marked edition_status: superseded — the identical requirement appears in the published AS/NZS 3500.1:2021 at Clause 5.3.5 (p.41), which also specifies 100 mm for a water service not exceeding DN 65.

answers.answer: Under AS 3500.1:2018, Clause 5.4.4(a), where water service pipes are located beneath concrete slabs on ground, pipes must be laid in a narrow trench on a bed of sand or fine-grained soil placed and compacted so as not to damage the piping, and "There shall be a minimum distance of 75 mm between the top of the pipe and the underside of the slab or slab-stiffening beam." So the minimum distance is 75 mm. Note: the 2018 edition held in the library is marked edition_status: superseded — in the library's published AS/NZS 3500.1:2021 the same requirement appears (re-worded only as "conform to") at Clause 5.5.4(a), p.48, and also states 75 mm.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2018, Clause 5.4.4(c), pipework that penetrates a slab on ground must be at right angles to the slab surface and "lagged for the full depth of the slab penetration with— (i) an impermeable flexible material of not less than 6 mm thickness; or (ii) impermeable plastics sleeve or conduit providing equivalent protection." The minimum thickness of impermeable flexible lagging is therefore 6 mm (an impermeable plastics sleeve or conduit giving equivalent protection is an accepted alternative). Note: the 2018 edition held in the knowledge base is marked superseded; the same 6 mm figure also appears in the published AS/NZS 3500.1:2021 at Clause 5.5.4(c)(i), p.48.

answers.answer: Under AS 3500.1:2018 Clause 8.4.1 (General), provision for removal of sludge must be made at the base of a water storage tank where the capacity exceeds 500 L: "Where the capacity exceeds 500 L, provision shall be made at the base for removal of sludge." The library also holds Clause 8.7 (sludge valves, p.68), which states "A sludge valve shall be fitted where the capacity of the tank exceeds 500 L. The minimum size of the valve shall be not less than half the outlet pipe size nor less than DN 40." Note: the 2018 edition held in the library is marked superseded; the current AS/NZS 3500.1:2021 edition in the library repeats the same 500 L threshold at Clause 8.4.1, p.70.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2018 Clause 8.4.4.3 (Discharge not readily visible), where the tank overflow pipe does not discharge to a readily visible position, a telltale pipe not smaller than DN 20 must be connected to the invert of the overflow pipe and discharge as required by Clause 8.4.4.2. The minimum telltale pipe size is therefore DN 20. Note: the library holds this document as superseded (edition_status: superseded), so the figure is quoted from the 2018 edition as asked, not as the current requirement.

answers.answer: Under Clause 18.3.1 (Hydrostatic test) of AS/NZS 3500.1:2018, a water service must not show any leakage when subjected to a hydrostatic pressure of 1500 kPa for a period of not less than 30 min. The clause also requires the test to be performed on installed piping prior to burial or concealment (and, for pipe systems with elastomeric seals, the piping backfilled leaving joints exposed until completion of the test). Note: the library's file for this edition carries edition_status 'superseded' — the text is the 2018 edition, which has since been superseded (the library holds a later 2021 edition of AS/NZS 3500.1).

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, Clause 2.4.2(d) requires that copper alloy bends and junctions used at the base of stacks greater than 9 m in height shall be cast or hot-pressed. Note the edition: the library's copy of AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 is marked edition_status: superseded, so this clause reflects the 2018 edition only; the library also holds AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, which should be checked for current work. (Related: Clause 2.4.3(b) deals with fabricated copper bends and junctions at the base of stacks up to 9 m, which shall be formed of Type B or heavier gauge copper — a different case from the one asked.)

answers.answer: Clause 4.6.6.6 of AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 requires a minimum height of 150 mm between the top of the overflow gully riser and the lowest fixture connected to the drain. The height is measured vertically from the overflow level of the gully riser (or the invert level of the overflow pipe) to the point of measurement for the fixture type given in Table 4.6.6.6 — e.g. top surface level of the water seal for a soil fixture with an integral trap, top surface level of the grate for a floor waste gully or shower, overflow rim for a soil fixture in an outbuilding graded to an external doorway, and top surface level of the fixture outlet for other fixtures (including greywater diversion devices).

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, an untrapped waste pipe discharging to the riser of a floor waste gully is limited to a maximum length of 1.2 m, as set out in Table 4.6.7.2 (column 'Fixture untrapped — Connected to riser of floor waste gully'), which gives 1.2 m for the untrapped fixtures listed (bain-marie/sterilizer, bar sink, bath, shower/bath, bidet, cleaners' sink, clothes-washing machine, laundry and ablution trough, refrigerated cabinet, shower). Clause 4.6.7.3 makes the table value mandatory: each fixture or fixture pair connected to a floor waste gully must have a separate waste pipe at a grade of not less than 2.5% 'and with a length not exceeding that specified in Table 4.6.7.2'. Caveats in the same table: an untrapped basin or drinking fountain is 'Not permitted' to a floor waste gully riser, a tundish is allowed 10.0 m, and connection to a submerged inlet floor waste gully is generally limited to trapped fixtures (2.5 m; see Figure 4.6.7.2, which shows the waste '2.5 m long max.'). Note the edition held is AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, which is superseded (a 2021 edition is in the library and a 2025 edition exists); the 1.2 m figure is the 2018 requirement.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 Clause 6.8.1(a), for stacks of three floor levels or more, no connection shall be made closer than 2.5 m downstream or 1 m upstream of the base of the stack. So the minimum distance downstream from the base of the stack is 2.5 m. The same clause also requires that no discharge pipe connecting a fixture upstream of a junction that connects a stack to a drain or graded pipe shall be closer than 1 m from the base of the stack. Note: the library edition is superseded (AS/NZS 3500.2:2018), and Figure 6.8.1 on p.84 confirms the 2.5 m and 1 m dimensions for the three-floor-level case.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, Clause 9.2.5, the distance is 2.4 m: "Where the distance between the invert of the drain or graded pipe and the lowest floor level exceeds 2.4 m, that floor shall be counted as an additional floor level." The same clause requires the maximum number of floor levels through which the stack passes (as specified in Tables 9.7.1(A), 9.7.1(B), 9.7.2(A) and 9.7.2(B)) to be counted from the point at which the stack connects to the drain or graded pipe and the highest floor level on which a fixture is connected. Figure 9.2.5 on the same page illustrates examples of floor level counting, marking the condition "If > 2.4 m (See Clause 9.2.5)". Edition note: the cited file carries edition_status "superseded" — it is the 2018 edition, not the current edition of AS/NZS 3500.2; the library front matter names the superseding edition, so check it before relying on this figure for current work.

Note: the library file for this clause is marked edition_status: superseded — AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 has been superseded (the library also holds the 2021 edition), so confirm the current edition before applying it to a current project.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, Clause 9.8.7.2 (Steep offsets), a waste stack of up to DN 100 may have steep offsets between the highest and lowest graded pipes connected, provided the listed requirements are met. Item (a) states: "Where the fixtures are unvented in accordance with Item (g), the maximum fixture unit loading to discharge to the stack shall not exceed 120 fixture units." (Note: the cross-reference in Item (a) points to Item (g), which deals with unvented single waste fixture discharge pipes and their maximum length per Table 9.5.1.) The maximum loading is therefore 120 fixture units. The edition used is AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, which is marked edition_status: superseded in this library — check the current edition before applying this figure.

answers.answer: Under Clause 9.9.5 (Graded offsets) of AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, a DN 100 stack with a graded offset installed between the base of the stack and the highest connection is limited to a stack height of not more than 10 consecutive floor levels. Clause 9.9.5 states: 'DN 100 stacks may be offset between the base of the stack and the highest connection, provided the following requirements are met: (a) Only one graded offset shall be installed in any stack. (b) The height of the stack shall not exceed 10 consecutive floor levels.' So the maximum is 10 consecutive floor levels, and only one graded offset is permitted in the stack. Note the edition used is superseded: this file carries edition_status 'superseded' (AS/NZS 3500.2:2018); the library does not hold a current 2025 edition for this clause, so confirm the figure against the current edition before relying on it.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, Clause 9.9.5 applies to a DN 100 stack with a graded offset between the base of the stack and the highest connection: only one graded offset may be installed, the stack may not exceed 10 consecutive floor levels, and the minimum distance between the centre-lines of the two vertical sections of the stack is 2 m — Clause 9.9.5(c) states "The minimum distance between the centre-lines of the vertical sections of the stack shall be 2 m." Do not confuse this with the 1 m figure in Clause 9.8.7.1(b), which applies to a waste stack up to DN 100 with a graded offset between the highest and lowest connections (the variations in Clause 9.8), not to the DN 100 base-to-highest-connection case asked about here. Note: the library file is the superseded 2018 edition; AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 is held in the library and a 2025 edition was published, so confirm against the current edition before use.

answers.answer: AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, Clause 12.8.6 (Venting) requires the holding tank to have a vent of minimum size DN 50, conforming with the venting requirements for waste fixtures, and the vent must be positioned a minimum of 100 mm above the waste inlet. The clause reads: "The holding tank shall be provided with a vent having a minimum size of DN 50 and shall conform with the venting requirements for waste fixtures. The vent shall be positioned a minimum of 100 mm above the waste inlet." Note that in the library text the watermark line "Accessed by TAFE NSW (TAFE Library Services) on 21 Dec 2018" is interleaved mid-sentence between "positioned a" and "minimum of 100 mm", so check the printed page p.166 to confirm the wording. Do not confuse this with Clause 12.6.3 (p.165), which is a different item — the wet well vent, minimum DN 80. The 2018 edition held in the library is marked superseded; if you are working to the current edition, verify the figures against the newer edition.

answers.answer: Under Clause 15.1 of AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, sanitary fixtures are tested by subjecting them to normal use, and after each test the residual water seal in the trap of the fixture concerned (or in any other trap connected to the same system) must, under normal operating conditions, retain a water seal of not less than 25 mm. Where a 25 mm seal cannot be retained, the system must be inspected, modified/repaired and the fixture retested until it conforms. Note: the 2018 edition held in the library is marked as superseded — the current published edition in the library is AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, whose Clause 15.1 (p.189) contains the same 25 mm requirement.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, Clause 15.2(a), when hydrostatic (water) testing is used on sanitary drainage, the pipe shall be filled with water "for sanitary drainage, to a height of not less than 1 m above the soffit level at the highest point of the section being tested". answers.answer: Under clause 6.3.5.2(f)(iii)(B) of AS/NZS 3500.3:2018, for pipes of 'all other materials' the bedding for an earth foundation 'shall be not less than 75 mm thick' — i.e. minimum bedding thickness of 75 mm where a site stormwater drain is laid on an earth foundation. (For comparison in the same clause: rock foundations require not less than 100 mm bedding with haunch support not less than 75 mm, and cement mortar bedding in rock/shale at gradients steeper than 1:5 requires a minimum depth of 50 mm below the bottom of the pipe.) Note also that clause 6.3.5.2(a)–(e) refers bedding/installation for specific pipe materials (e.g. PVC to AS/NZS 2032) to those standards; the 75 mm earth-foundation figure applies to the 'all other materials' case in 6.3.5.2(f).

Note: the edition used, AS/NZS 3500.3:2018, is marked superseded in the library (the latest published edition held is AS/NZS 3500.3:2021), so this figure should be confirmed against the 2021 edition before use.

answers.answer: For an underground OSD tank with open storage zones, the tank floor must be graded at a minimum slope of 1:140 towards the outlet, to minimise ponding and depositing of debris. (The 1:60 / 1:100 slopes at Appendix N12 are for above-ground landscaped storages, not underground tanks.)

answers.answer: No — the 300 mm figure is not what Clause 3.6.7 states. Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, Clause 3.6.7 ('Crossover of underground services', p.33), where an underground drain crosses a service (or an underground service crosses a drain), the three requirements are: (a) the crossing must be "at an angle of not less than 45°"; (b) it must "have a vertical separation of not less than 100 mm"; and (c) it must "be marked along its length for 1 m either side of the centre-line of the service with marker tape laid 150 mm above the installed service." So the minimum vertical separation at a crossover is 100 mm, not 300 mm. The 300 mm figure you are thinking of appears in Clause 3.6.6 ('Separation from other underground services', p.32), which is a different situation (separation, not crossover) and reads: "The separation between any underground drain and any other service other than electrical supply cables, consumer gas piping, communication service or water service shall be at least 100 mm or 300 mm from a stormwater drain exceeding DN 100." That 300 mm applies to a stormwater drain exceeding DN 100, not to a general service crossover under 3.6.7. Note also Clause 3.6.8 (p.33): drains must have at least 100 mm clearance from underground obstructions.

answers.answer: AS/NZS 3500.1:2025 is not held in the knowledge base — the latest edition held is AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, so no 2025 figure can be given. For information only, the 2021 edition (published, not superseded) states at Clause 8.3.3 Access (p.70): 'Headroom and side access shall be provided for every tank to enable inspection, cleaning and maintenance procedures to be carried out to the interior and exterior of the tank. Where the interior depth of any storage tank exceeds 2 m, access ladders shall be installed.' NOTE 1 to that clause refers to AS 2865 for confined spaces and NOTE 2 to AS 1657 for the design, construction and installation of fixed platforms, walkways, stairways and ladders. So under the held 2021 edition, a tank with an interior depth greater than 2 m requires access ladders to be installed, in addition to headroom and side access for every tank. The 2021 text no longer uses the older wording 'access ladders of standard design and dimensions complying with AS 1657' found in the superseded 2003, 2015 and 2018 editions (which also required headroom and side access), because AS 1657 is now a NOTE reference. Confirm the position under AS/NZS 3500.1:2025 against the published 2025 edition, which is outside this knowledge base.

For information only, the 2021 edition (published, not superseded) states in Clause 8.3.6 'Combined effective storage' that the minimum wet well storage between the high and low working levels 'expressed in cubic metres, shall be 1 % of the catchment area in m2 and not less than 3 m3'. The same clause also requires the combined effective storage (volume able to be pumped in 30 min plus the wet well storage) to be not less than the volume of run-off from the storm of 10 % AEP (10 years ARI) and duration of 120 min. Note the 2021 text is a slightly reworded version of the superseded 2018/2015 wording ('1% of the catchment area in m2; in any case it shall be not less than 3 m3'); the 2025 edition may differ and must be checked in the source document.
